answer: Each applicant seals one kernel of black rice in a vial keyed to its holder, then sends it on a voyage through twelve waystations across a river delta. Each station weighs the vial, notes the delta in moisture since the last reading, stamps the seal, and forwards it; each stamp derives from that delta plus the key, so stations follow in sequence and none can be skipped or doubled up. A forged vial fails: no two kernels share one grain pattern. One voyage costs $410 and 11 courier-days; 5,000 fakes need 5,000 vials, $2.05 million and 55,000 days, and no courier carries two voyages at once.
